text.p: These are the leading stories in the Belgrade press on Monday . Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
NASA BORBA
- Opposition coalition Zajedno (Together) marks sixth anniversary of violent Belgrade riots with rally, calls on authorities for dialogue.

- Although lectures at Belgrade University were officially to resume Monday, some students still waiting for verification of rector's resignation. Serbian education minister Jovo Todorovic says lost classes will be made up during summer.

- Montenegrin Prime Minister Milo Djukanovic on visit to Washington. Four Montenegrin cargo vessels to sail out of U.S. ports after five years of blockade. Despite Djukanovic's optimism on Montenegro's membership in the International Monetary Fund and World Bank, sources say international financial institutions deal only with sovereign states.
- Trial of Montenegrin opposition leaders Novak Kilibarda and Slavko Perovic for slandering the republic's leadership during election campaign continues.

- President of Serb region of Eastern Slavonia in Croatia Vojislav Stanimirovic says new exodus of Serbs must be prevented. Of around 160,000 Serbs in the region, some 60,000 are refugees from other parts of Craotia, says Stanimirovic.
- Banks issuing guarantees more readily than approving classical credits, but when payment time comes, fall into serious insolvency. Even well-off banks threatened by collapse.
- "What the chambers of commerce are calling for is a planned economy and that is unacceptable," says Yugoslav trade minister Djordje Siradovic.
POLITIKA

- General concensus needed for a long-term strategy of Yugoslavia's economic development, which would include liberalisation of trade, privatisation, position of the central bank and financial and banking systems, says Belgrade Economics Institute director Danko Djunic. "Exports key to development."
- Yugoslavia needs to invest $29 billion over the next 25 years in energy projects, of which around $20 billion in electric power.

- Serbia has around 1.5 million square metres of unused industrial capacities, mostly in production. Idle factory halls, warehouses, stores and hotels, including equipment, worth around two billion German marks.

- Staff of weekly NIN split over replacement of editor in chief Dusan Velickovic. Nineteen members of editorial board to go on strike Monday. NIN director Tomislav Dzadzic says strike illegal, threatens action against protesters.
BORBA
- On average around 759,144 people sought work per month in Serbia during 1996, indicating a rising unemployment rate of 18.2 percent compared to active work force, Serbia's labour office said.
- Yugoslav-Polish trade in 1996 worth more than $65 million.
- What will 1997 fiscal policy look like? Taxes higher, revenues dropping. In January only 1.2 billion dinars flowed into state coffers, or 31 percent less than in December 1996.
VECERNJE NOVOSTI

- Serb member of collective Bosnian Presidency Momcilo Krajisnik says agreement on special ties between the Bosnian Serb entity and Yugoslavia does not represent unification of two states and is not aimed against Bosnia-Herzegovina. -- Belgrade newsroom +381 11 222 4305
